posts.title: Your Villages Weekend + What's New: Rocky Rolls Brownwood
posts.date: September 3, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Morning, neighbors. The coffee is on and the cart is charged.

Labor Day is behind us and the squares are still humming. Here's the scoop on the upcoming weekend, plus a couple of new things worth knowing about.

What to do this weekend

First, the thing people keep getting wrong. Music does not start at five right now. Through September 30, nightly entertainment on all three squares runs 6:00 to 10:00 PM. They shifted the hours to dodge the afternoon heat. Show up at five and you'll be standing in an empty square with a cold drink. Ask me how I know.

Friday, September 4. Beauty & The Beats take Spanish Springs, 6 to 10 PM. Seventies, eighties, nineties, plus the one hit wonders you forgot you loved. Over at Lake Sumter Landing it's Scooter The DJ, same hours, and yes, he will make you participate. Brownwood gets AndrewLuv and the Franchise Players Band, soul and Motown and dance music, 6 to 10 PM.

Friday is my night for Spanish Springs. Get there by 5:15, grab a table on Main Street, eat first, then wander over. The square fills up fast once the band starts.

Saturday, September 5. This is the big one. Rocky and The Rollers are at Brownwood Paddock Square, 6 to 10 PM. Twenty seven years playing The Villages. They are a Villages institution for a reason, and the dance floor gets crowded early.

If Brownwood is not your direction, Lake Sumter Landing has The Fire Rhythms Band with Caribbean and Brazilian beats mixed into funk and Top 40. Spanish Springs goes club mode with CLUB CTRL Feat. DJ Lu-S. All three run 6 to 10 PM.

Eating near Brownwood on Saturday? Get there early. The Paddock Square restaurants back up around 5:30 when there's a name band on the bill. Trust me on this one.

Sunday, September 6. A softer landing. Sheila & The Sound bring Aretha and Journey to Spanish Springs. The Alex Hayes Band plays country rock and classic rock at Lake Sumter Landing. Brownwood has Scooter The DJ. Everything 6 to 10 PM.

Sunday is my favorite square night. Smaller crowds, easier parking, same music.

One note. The entertainment folks say all events and performances are subject to change, so peek at the schedule before you load up the cart.

What's new

LUXE Steakhouse and Cellar is coming, and soon. This one has my attention. It's a reservation only steakhouse from RGM Restaurants, the group behind Red Sauce, Mallory Hill and Glenview. It's going in at 1488 Craig Ct, on the Woodlands Country Club golf course. Owner Jack Suleiman told Business Debut he is targeting an opening by the end of September.

Here's what makes it interesting. They plan to cap the number of reservations they take each day. That means no rushing you out, which is rare around here. About 200 seats, 5,500 square feet, and an open bar with big sliding windows facing the course. Beef is coming from Meats by Linz, wagyu and dry aged and prime.

The catch, and it is a real one. Reservation only means you cannot pop in after golf. And construction was still six to eight weeks out as of mid August, so "end of September" may slide. I would not book a birthday dinner there yet.

Barons Creek Vineyards on Main Street. The Texas winery opened a tasting room at 1171 Main Street in Spanish Springs. They do a guided tasting where staff ask what you like first, then build a flight around it. Small bites too, pizzas and bruschetta and charcuterie. They also plan trivia, music bingo and paint and sip nights.

That last part is the real news for my crowd. A wine spot right on the square that does weeknight events is exactly what the girls and I have been asking for.

Susan's plan

Friday I'm eating early on Main Street and staying for Beauty & The Beats. Saturday I am at Brownwood for Rocky, and I am leaving the house by 5. Sunday, if it's not pouring, Lake Sumter Landing with a glass of wine and no agenda at all.

Pencil something in. The heat breaks eventually, but these bands are here now.

See you around the square,
Susan

By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Squares, Scams and a New Restaurant
posts.date: August 31, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Morning, neighbors. Coffee's on and the golf cart is charged.

Here's the scoop on the weekend that just wrapped. Three squares, live music every night, and a couple of little news items worth knowing.

The music ran late, and that's on purpose

Quick reminder if you keep showing up at five. Through September 30, nightly entertainment on the squares runs 6:00 to 10:00, not 5:00 to 9:00. They shifted the hours to duck the worst of the summer heat. Same four hours of music, just pushed back an hour.

Friday, Lake Sumter Landing had Radlin' Rootz, an eclectic cover and original band. Spanish Springs had The Brothers Jukebox doing country and classic rock. Brownwood had Bar Fly working the '70s and '80s, and Eastport had Zee-R, an artist out of Brazil.

Saturday was the interesting one. September Dogs, the four piece female fronted band, played both Spanish Springs and Lake Sumter Landing. Stella Beat brought a Latin and Top 40 set to Eastport.

Sunday, Johnny Wild & the Delights closed out Lake Sumter Landing with '50s and '60s material. Eighteen87 had Spanish Springs.

If you like knowing who's playing before you park, the square pages above are the ones I keep bookmarked. Trust me on this one.

A new restaurant is coming to Rolling Acres

Food news. Villages-News reported Saturday that a Mediterranean restaurant is moving into the old Moe's spot at Rolling Acres Plaza.

That space has been sitting empty and it's a good corner. I have not eaten there, obviously, nobody has yet. But I'll be first in line when they open, and I'll report back honestly.

The one you actually need to hear

This is the who-knew note of the week, and it's a good one.

The Lady Lake police chief put out a warning Saturday about a "Back the Badge" fundraising scam making the rounds. People calling and asking for money on behalf of police.

Real departments do not cold call you for donations. If someone does, hang up and call the department yourself using the number on their website. Tell your neighbor with the big heart and the checkbook. I sent my own.

Housekeeping around the districts

Three small things worth a note on the fridge.

  • Trash pickup shifts for some of us over the Labor Day holiday. Check whether your day changed before you roll the can out.
  • The Colony sports pool is closed for pressure washing. If that's your water volleyball spot, plan a backup.
  • The Blue Heron adult pool is getting new furniture. Small thing. Nice thing. Those loungers had earned their retirement.

Looking ahead

If you want something on the calendar, Rock of ABBA comes to town September 3. Ticketed, so grab yours before the girls do.

That's the honest version of the weekend. Music was steady, news was quiet, and the biggest story was a phone scam. I'll take a quiet weekend in August.

Now go enjoy yourself.

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Music, Golf and a Steakhouse
posts.date: August 24, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Good Monday, friends. Pour the coffee, then let's talk about the weekend.

It was a quieter one, no big festival, no street closures. But the squares did what they always do. They filled up anyway.

The squares kept the lights on

Here's the scoop on music. The squares run live bands every single night, and this weekend was no exception. Villages-News listed the lineup all three days, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Groove Slayers led off Friday's listing, The Voodoo Gypsies got the Saturday spotlight, and Dance Express closed out Sunday.

Saturday night was the busy one. Per The Villages Entertainment, Spanish Springs had a party band from 6 to 10, country rock and classic rock across a few decades. Over at Lake Sumter Landing, same hours, but old school, Motown and top 40. Brownwood was the quiet square Saturday, no band listed.

My advice if you missed it. Pick your square by the music, not by habit. Two very different nights, ten minutes apart in a cart.

A steakhouse worth putting on your calendar

Now for the food news, and this one is a real one. Villages-News reported Saturday that the new restaurant coming to The Villages will be reservations only. That's LUXE Steakhouse & Cellar, out at the Woodlands golf course.

The Villages announced it as prime steaks, a real wine cellar and tableside presentations. The plan is lunch and dinner, seven days a week. Contractors were still working as of mid August, with the opening aimed at the end of September.

Reservations only is the part people will grumble about. I'll say it gently. It also means no forty minute wait on a Friday. I'll take that trade.

Golf, and a nice one

The Silver Rockettes had a day of golf at Bacall Executive over the weekend, and Villages-News ran the photo. Bacall is a good pick for a group like that, short, friendly, no ego required.

This is your reminder that the clubs here are not hard to join. They are hard to hear about. If you have been meaning to find your people, a golf group is the easiest door.

One heads up for today. Villages-News noted that two golf courses are closed Monday. Check before you load the clubs.

The who knew note

Here's the one I'd actually clip and save. There's a Senior Traffic Safety Class coming up, and it covers roundabouts and golf cart rules.

I know. You've driven a cart for eleven years. So have I. I also watched three people take a roundabout three different ways last Thursday, and only one of them was right. A free refresher never hurt anybody, and it's a good excuse to bring a neighbor who won't sign up alone. Trust me on this one.

Honest note

That's what I could confirm this weekend. No festival, no grand opening ribbon, no big charity walk. Some weekends in late August are just hot and easy, and there is nothing wrong with that. I'd rather tell you five true things than pad it out.

If you did something worth knowing about, tell me. I'll chase it down for next Monday.

See you around the square,
Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Rocky, Brass and a Market
posts.date: August 17, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Good Monday, friends. Pour the coffee, then let's talk about the weekend.

Three full nights of music on the squares, one very good Saturday morning, and a couple of things worth writing on your calendar. Here's the scoop.

Friday warmed us up

Everything kicked off at 6 o'clock. Uncle Bob's Rock Shop took Brownwood Paddock Square and the Zee-R Band had Spanish Springs. Lake Sumter Landing did something a little different with CLUB CTRL featuring DJ Lu-S. Sawgrass Grove had The Edge Of Rock, and Eastport had The Brothers Jukebox.

If 6 p.m. still feels late to you, that is on purpose. Summer hours run 6 to 10 through September 30 instead of the usual 5 to 9, to duck the worst of the heat. I have come around on it. You eat at a civilized hour and the band is still playing when the sun finally quits.

Saturday was the big one

Start with the morning. Hometown Market runs every Saturday at Brownwood, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., and they post a fresh vendor map each week. Produce, baked goods, jewelry, and the sort of yard and golf cart odds and ends you did not know you needed. Golf car parking is on Kiessel Road and W Torch Lake Drive. Park there and save yourself the circling.

Then the night. Rocky and The Rollers were at Spanish Springs, which is never a hard sell. The Voodoo Gypsies had Brownwood, The Dave Capp Project had Lake Sumter Landing, and Cable Cars played Eastport. Sawgrass Grove pulled a double: Acoustic Blue at noon, Paisley Craze at 6.

Sunday eased us out

Dance Express at Brownwood, Paradise at Lake Sumter Landing, Sheila & The Sound at Spanish Springs, SSnakeyez at Sawgrass Grove, and Bourbon Street Brass out at Eastport. Brass on a Sunday evening is a fine way to close a weekend.

And somebody was up early enough to catch the sunrise over Spanish Springs and send the photo in. Bless them, because it was not me.

For the thirsty

The bar huts are pouring a Berry Ripple all month. Raspberry, pineapple, vodka. Eight dollars for a single, $10.50 for a double, while supplies last. August is going fast, so do not dawdle.

Restaurant news worth filing

Culver's is planning a third location in the area, on 2.87 acres at 945 N. U.S. Hwy. 27/441 in Lady Lake, the old BB&T Bank site. Nothing to eat there yet, so temper your expectations. But if the Southern Trace location has ever tested your patience on a Friday, you understand why I am bringing it up.

The who-do-I-call note

Here is one I would not have found on my own. The Villages Fun Fitness Table Tennis Club runs table tennis sessions for residents with Parkinson's, along with their care partners and spouses, in the Delores Del Rio room at La Hacienda Recreation Center. Roughly two dozen people a week. They have since opened it up to residents with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families. If somebody on your street has been looking for a reason to get out of the house, that is a phone call worth making.

Two practical notes while I have you. The pickleball courts at Franklin Recreation Center close for maintenance Monday, Aug. 24 through Thursday, Aug. 27. Their number is (352) 674-1989. Plan your morning game accordingly, because I certainly am.

And the gopher tortoises at the Harold S. Schwartz Wildlife Preserve over in Santiago are doing so well they have run clean out of room. CDD 2 is trying to sort out what to do about it. Only in Florida is "too many tortoises" a genuine agenda item.

That is the weekend. Not a blockbuster, but a good one.

See you around the square,
Susan

By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Brass on the Square
posts.date: August 10, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Good Monday morning, friends. Pour the coffee, because we have some catching up to do. The squares were humming all three nights, a heron made the local paper, and one street over by Lake Sumter is quietly minting millionaires. Here's the scoop.

Brass on the boardwalk

Lake Sumter Landing had itself a weekend. Friday night The 789s got things rolling, five musicians from five corners of the country playing rock, disco and pop until ten. Saturday brought Bourbon Street Brass and those big New Orleans horns to the square. If you read last week's post, you know I pointed Gloria and her pickleball gentleman to that exact show for their first date. No word back yet. I am choosing to take that as a very good sign.

Sunday, Pavani's Band closed out the weekend with a night of '70s and '80s hits by the water. A reminder for the newer folks: summer hours on the squares run 6 to 10 p.m. through September 30, so there's plenty of daylight left for dinner first and dancing second. The bar huts are also pouring their August special, the Berry Ripple, raspberry and pineapple with vodka, 8 dollars for a single and 10.50 for a double. That one sounds like a front porch in a cup.

A million-dollar street

Villages-News reported Saturday that a home in Bridgeport at Lake Sumter sold for 1.1 million dollars. By Sunday they were reporting that another home on the very same street crossed the million-dollar mark, selling for double its original purchase price. Two in one weekend. My house has the same sunshine and better tomatoes, so I can only assume my number is coming.

The library that turned late fees into pencils

Here's a who-knew for you. The Lady Lake Library donated school supplies through its annual fine forgiveness program, per Villages-News on Sunday. Local kids head back to class with fresh supplies, and a few overdue consciences around here got wiped clean in the bargain. Everybody wins. If your grandkids are nearby, a library card is still the best free thing in town.

Small news, good news

The Collier swimming pool is getting new furniture, which I count as a genuine quality of life improvement for anyone who has ever fought over the last good lounger. And the weekend photo pages were showing off, with a sunrise near Ednas' on the Green and a great blue heron wrestling down a large eel along the Hogeye Pathway. That bird ate better than some of us this weekend, and I include myself.

Tonight, if you're up for it

Blonde Ambition plays Brownwood with their Top 40, Motown and everything-else show, and The Rundown Band brings '80s rock to Lake Sumter Landing, 6 to 10 as always. Monday is the new Saturday when you're retired.

That's the weekend as it actually happened, no padding, no fluff. If you spotted something I missed, or you know which square band deserves a shout next week, send it my way. My little black book always has room for one more page.

See you around the square,
Susan

By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider

posts.title: Ask Susan: Which Square Wins for a First Date?
posts.date: August 6, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Well, friends, we're doing something a little different this week. The mailbag is open, and one of your neighbors got right to the good stuff:

Gloria from the Village of Pennecamp asks: "A very nice gentleman from my pickleball group finally worked up the nerve to ask me to dinner. It's my first date in — let's just say a while. Which square should we pick? I don't want anything too loud, but I don't want us sitting there in silence, either."

Gloria, honey, first of all: good for you. Second of all, you've come to the right woman. The girls will tell you I have strong opinions on this subject, and I'm rarely wrong. Here's the scoop.

The golden rule of square dates

All summer long — June 1 through September 30 — the free nightly entertainment on the squares runs 6 to 10 p.m. instead of the usual 5 to 9. That later start is a gift for a first date: dinner first, music second. You get a proper conversation over a meal while it's still quiet, and then the band gives you something to do when the small talk runs thin. Nobody has ever needed a backup plan while a live band is playing. Trust me on this one.

My pick: Lake Sumter Landing

For a first date, it's Lake Sumter Landing, and it isn't close. The water, the lights, the stroll along the boardwalk when you want a quieter moment away from the stage — no other square gives you an escape hatch that pretty. And this Saturday, August 8, the entertainment gods are on your side: Bourbon Street Brass brings New Orleans brass and jazz to the square from 6 to 10. Romantic without trying too hard, lively without shouting over guitar solos. That's the sweet spot, Gloria.

The supporting cast

If your gentleman turns out to be a dancer, Saturday at Spanish Springs is The Fire Rhythms Band — Caribbean and Brazilian beats, funk, and Top 40, a full-blown dance party. First dates have been made on less. And if Saturday doesn't work, Sunday the 9th at Brownwood has September Dogs, a female-fronted four-piece with lovely layered vocals — a gentler landing if you'd rather ease into things.

One more trick up my sleeve

Get there before the band. The bar huts open at 4 with happy hour from 5 to 6, per Villages-News — and August's special is the Berry Ripple, raspberry and pineapple with vodka, $8 for a single. Hand him one of those at golden hour by the water and let the evening do the rest. And Gloria? Wear the good earrings. He noticed you at pickleball; he'll notice those too.

Got a question for me? Send it through the "Ask Susan" box over at thevillagesfood.com — the mailbag is open, and no question is too small, too silly, or too spicy. See you on the square.

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend + What's New: Brass, Burgers & Soft Serve
posts.date: July 23, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Well, we made it to another Thursday, friends. The girls and I already have our Saturday mapped out, and I'm here to share the homework so you don't have to do it. Here's the scoop on the weekend ahead — plus a few changes around town you'll want to know about.

One housekeeping note before we start: square music runs 6 to 10 p.m. all summer, through September 30. Later start, cooler evening. I call that a win.

What to do this weekend

Friday, July 24. Three squares, three very different nights. Penta, a rock, blues, and funk band out of Daytona Beach, takes Spanish Springs. Over at Lake Sumter Landing, it's Bandemic — forty-plus years of rock 'n' roll, from classic '80s to country-rock. And Brownwood is doing something different: CLUB CTRL with DJ Lu-S, a full-on DJ dance party under the lights. If the grandkids are visiting, take them to Brownwood. They'll be shocked you know what a DJ is.

Saturday, July 25. This is my pick of the weekend: Swing Theory at Brownwood. Seven pieces, big band sounds from the '20s, '30s, and '40s, plus jazz, blues, and Latin. Wear shoes you can actually dance in. Trust me on this one. Prefer classic rock? Uncle Bob's Rock Shop plays Lake Sumter Landing with a real concert feel. And Spanish Springs gets the Zee-R Band, family-friendly hits from all eras, fronted by an artist originally from Brazil.

Sunday, July 26. End the weekend easy. Bourbon Street Brass brings New Orleans brass and jazz to Spanish Springs — get there early with a to-go dinner and a lawn chair. Sheila & The Sound covers everything from Aretha to Journey at Lake Sumter Landing, and Dance Express plays Motown and old school at Brownwood.

Two quick dining notes. Eat before the music or grab something on the square — every one of these squares has plenty within walking distance of the stage. And the bar huts are pouring their July special, the Freedom Punch, $8 for a single, while supplies last. It's red, white, and blue and it goes down easy on a hot night. You're welcome.

What's new around town

The hottest line in town is for ice cream. The new Twistee Treat at Pinellas Plaza opened at the end of June, and the drive-up lane has been wrapping around that big 25-foot cone building after dark. They're open until 10:30 every night — which makes it the perfect stop on the cart ride home from the square. I'm not saying I've been twice this week. I'm not saying I haven't.

Three new spots coming to the Market at Sawgrass Grove. FMK Hospitality is adding three fast-casual concepts: Sizzle 'N Smash (smash burgers and milkshakes), Southern Tender (chicken tenders and fries), and Papa Joe's Pizza and More (pizza by the slice). FMK already runs Luma at the Market, so they know the room. I'll report back once the fryers are on.

Goodbye to an original. Sad news from the south side: the Fenney Grill closed its doors as of Sunday, July 19. It opened back in 2017 as the very first eatery in that part of The Villages, when Fenney felt like the frontier. Nine years is a good run, and plenty of us have a sunset dinner memory from that porch. Raise a glass.

A new ER is open near Colony Plaza. File this under things you hope you never need: the new AdventHealth freestanding ER began seeing patients on July 21 — 12 patient rooms and board-certified emergency physicians, right on the 466 corridor. Put it in the back of your mind next to your other who-do-I-call notes.

That's the week, neighbors. Music every night, ice cream until 10:30, and a new reason to visit Sawgrass Grove on the way. Pencil it in.

See you around the square,
— Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Rock at Brownwood, Goodbye Fenney Grill
posts.date: July 20, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Morning, neighbors. Grab your coffee — here's the scoop on the weekend we just wrapped up.

It was a quieter July weekend by Villages standards. Hot, a little stormy in the afternoons, and the squares carried the show. But we did lose an old friend on the dining side. More on that in a minute.

Brownwood had the beat all weekend

Brownwood Paddock Square ran the table Friday through Sunday, per the official Brownwood entertainment calendar.

Friday night belonged to Rocky and The Rollers. Twenty-seven years playing The Villages, and they still pack the square. If you were there, you know. The dance floor filled before the first song ended.

Saturday brought The Voodoo Gypsies, the classic rock crew out of Central Florida. Rock 'n roll hits from the '60s, '70s, and '80s, exactly the way we like them.

Sunday wound things down with Daisy Fever, taking us from Woodstock to Studio 54. Folk, soul, disco, and classic rock. A nice mellow-to-groovy finish for the weekend.

Quick reminder while we're at it: through September 30, square music runs 6 to 10 p.m. instead of the usual 5 to 9. That's the official summer-hours shift to dodge the worst of the heat and the afternoon storms. Plan your golf cart ride accordingly.

We said goodbye to the Fenney Grill

Here's the bittersweet one. The Fenney Grill served its last meals Sunday, July 19, according to Villages-News.com.

If you live down south, you remember what that place meant. It opened in 2017 as the first restaurant in the Fenney area, back when that end of The Villages felt like the frontier. Plenty of us had our first meal south of 44 right there on that porch.

The writing had been on the wall — they'd cut back to summer hours in May, and it's been a bumpy stretch since. I won't pile on. I'll just say thanks for nine years of burgers with a view, and I'll keep my ears open for what moves into that spot. You'll hear it here first.

One for the road

If you're headed to a square this week, the bar huts are pouring their July special, the red-white-and-blue Freedom Punch, $8 for a single, while supplies last. Details on the bar hut page. It's as patriotic as a drink gets, and it goes down easy on a 90-degree evening. Trust me on this one.

That's the weekend, friends. A little music, a little farewell, a lot of humidity. This week's lineup is already posted on the entertainment calendars — Paradise plays Brownwood tonight and Rocky and The Rollers slide over to Lake Sumter Landing.

See you around the square,
— Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Clark Barrios, Storm Skies & More
posts.date: July 13, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Happy Monday, neighbors. Grab your coffee — here's the scoop on the weekend we just had.

First, a housekeeping note if you haven't been out to the squares lately. Summer hours are still in effect — music runs 6 to 10 p.m. through the end of September, per The Villages Entertainment. That extra hour past nine takes some getting used to. But it beats melting at 5 o'clock. Trust me on this one.

Friday night: DJ night at Brownwood

Friday, Brownwood Paddock Square went full club mode with DJ Lu-S spinning until 10. Not everybody's cup of tea, I know. But the younger crowd — and by younger I mean the 60-somethings — seems to love a DJ night. The Greg Warren Trio held down the south end of town with their country and classic rock mix.

Saturday: a full slate on the squares

Saturday was the big one. The Clark Barrios Band played Brownwood — six pieces, big vocals, the kind of rhythm section that gets golf carts parked early. Over at Spanish Springs, Zee-R brought his family-friendly classics from all eras. He's originally from Brazil, and his shows always draw a friendly crowd. And Lake Sumter Landing had a homegrown Villages rock band cranking out classic rock favorites right in my backyard.

Mother Nature put on her own show Saturday night, too. If you saw those clouds flickering over Lake Sumter, you weren't imagining it — Villages-News caught the nighttime storm clouds lighting up over Lake Sumter Landing. July in Florida, folks. Keep the rain jacket in the cart.

While you're at the square: Freedom Punch

Here's one for my fellow snackers and sippers. The bar huts on the squares are pouring a Freedom Punch all July — red, white, and blue, served over ice, $8 for a single and $10.50 for a double, while supplies last. The Tequila Sunrise is still on the menu at the same price if punch isn't your thing. You're welcome.

The end of an era

Some real hometown news from the weekend: Villages-News reported Saturday that our hometown bank has officially changed ownership. An end of an era for a lot of us who've banked there since we unpacked our first moving box. I'll keep an ear out on what changes — if anything — for us regulars.

One from Susan's little black book

Filed under “who knew?” — there's a free program to learn safe internet browsing open to residents. With all the scam calls and phishing emails going around, this one's worth an hour of your time. I sent my own neighbor. Details are in the Villages-News writeup.

And a little something for the bird lovers: a Villages-News photographer caught a swallow-tailed kite feeding on a midair catch over Sawgrass Grove this weekend. Gorgeous shot. Worth a click.

Looking ahead this week

Tonight it's X Girlfriend at Brownwood, Big Chief at Spanish Springs, Earth Beat at Lake Sumter Landing, and live band karaoke at Eastport — yes, you singing with a real band behind you. And Sawgrass Grove has Boozy Bingo tonight and free Trivia Tuesday at noon tomorrow.

That's the weekend, friends. Short, sweet, and true.

See you around the square,
— Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend + What's New: Soul at the Savannah
posts.date: July 9, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Here's the scoop, friends. July is doing its July thing — steamy afternoons, quick storms, and that golden hour when the squares come alive. The good news? Nightly entertainment runs 6 to 10 p.m. all summer now, pushed back an hour to dodge the heat. Smart move. That's one more hour for dinner before the dancing starts.

What to do this weekend

Friday night: pick your square. At Spanish Springs, Bandemic takes the stage from 6 to 10 with forty-plus years of rock, from classic '80s to country-rock. Down at Brownwood, The Brothers Jukebox brings country gold and classic rock harmonies, same hours. I lean Brownwood on Fridays. Grab an early table on the square, then wander over when the band kicks in.

Saturday morning: the farmers market. The Brownwood Farmers Market runs Saturday from 9 to 1 — summer hours, so go early before the produce wilts and so do you. Fresh vegetables, local honey, baked goods. I never leave empty-handed. Trust me on this one.

Saturday night: the big one. A Decade of Soul plays the Savannah Center on Saturday. This is the Motown and '70s soul tribute that ran more than 1,600 shows in Times Square before finding its way to us. Aretha, Marvin, James Brown — the whole songbook. It's ticketed, so check times and grab seats through The Villages Entertainment before it sells through.

Rather stay outside Saturday? The Edge Of Rock — a homegrown Villages rock band — plays Spanish Springs, and the Zee-R Band covers classic hits at Brownwood, both 6 to 10.

Sunday: ease into it. Think Big Band plays Spanish Springs from 6 to 10 — classic rock, Motown, blues, country, they play it all. Over at Brownwood, the Alex Hayes Band brings high-energy country rock. A Sunday supper near either square, then an hour or two of music? That's my kind of weekend landing.

One more thing while you're out there: the bar huts are pouring a Freedom Punch special through July — red, white, and blue in a cup, $8 single. You're welcome.

What's new

More food coming to The Market at Sawgrass Grove. This is the one I'm excited about. FMK — the folks behind Luma Mediterranean Kitchen — announced three new food spots for the Market: Sizzle 'N Smash for smash burgers and milkshakes, Southern Tender for chicken tenders and fries, and Papa Joe's Pizza and More with pizza by the slice. Luma won me over on the first visit, so I have high hopes. The grandkids will be thrilled about the milkshakes. So will I, frankly.

Zunzibar is open in Middleton. A new restaurant called Zunzibar opened in Middleton late last month. I haven't made it down yet, but it's on my list. If you've been, tell me what to order.

The new Walmart on 466 is open. The new Walmart in Lady Lake opened June 24 at the Hammock Oaks development on County Road 466, and the early birds were out in force. Handy if you're on the north side. The parking lot is still finding its rhythm, so maybe skip the Saturday noon rush.

That's the weekend, neighbors. Music every night, soul on Saturday, and burgers on the horizon. Pencil it in.

See you around the square,
— Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Rocky, Jazz & a Warm One
posts.date: June 29, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Well, hello again. Pull up a chair. I hope you got out this weekend, because the squares were humming. It was a warm one — central Florida in late June, you know the drill — but the music didn't mind one bit. Here's the scoop on what I caught.

The squares were singing

Friday night I made my way down to Lake Sumter Landing, and who do I find but Rocky and The Rollers — 27 years of doing this in The Villages and still packing the dance floor. They closed out the weekend Sunday night too. If you like your oldies high-energy with a little doo-wop sparkle, those are your guys. Saturday the Landing switched it up with Osaka Fall, who run everything from old-school jams to glam rock and soulful slow ones. (Lake Sumter Landing schedule)

Over at Sawgrass Grove, Friday belonged to 3P, that acoustic trio that bounces between reggae, country and pop without missing a step. Saturday brought in Radlin' Rootz, an eclectic band of top-tier players out of Ocala. Those same Rootz folks turned up Sunday at Spanish Springs — so if you missed them one night, the square gods gave you a second chance. (Sawgrass Grove, Spanish Springs)

And Brownwood kept the Saturday crowd on their feet with a Motown-and-Top-40 set built for dancing. The squares run music every single night, 6 to 10, and it's free — still the best deal in town. (Live Square Entertainment)

A little something indoors, too

Not everyone wants to sweat through a square dance in June, and I don't blame you. Saturday night, Savannah Center hosted 3DN — The Ultimate 3 Dog Nite Tribute Show. If “Joy to the World” is still on your car radio, that was the ticket. (Daily Sun calendar)

Here's my who-knew note for the weekend. Sunday evening, More Jazz brought the Rick Steuart Quartet to Colony Cottage Recreation Center. A quiet, classy night of jazz tucked into a rec center — that's the kind of thing folks live here for years and never try. Trust me on this one: the smaller rec-center shows are some of the best-kept secrets we've got. (events listing)

Eating around the music

I won't pretend I tracked down a brand-new restaurant opening this weekend — I didn't, and I won't make one up for you. But the squares make their own dinner plan. Grab a bite at the Landing or Sawgrass before the band starts, find a spot with a little shade, and let the night come to you. That's the move when it's this warm out.

Speaking of warm — let's be honest about it. We sat in the low-to-mid 90s all weekend with the usual afternoon thunderstorms rolling through. (AccuWeather) Keep water in the cart, find the late-day breeze, and don't fight the heat — outlast it. The music doesn't get going till the sun's on its way down anyway.

Looking ahead

If you're already itching for the week, 1776 the Musical takes the stage at Savannah Center tonight, Monday, at 7. (Daily Sun calendar) A little patriotic warm-up before the Fourth.

That's what I could confirm from a warm, music-filled weekend. Quieter on the big-event front, but the squares carried it like they always do. Now go enjoy yourself.

See you around the square,
— Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend + What's New: Rocky's Back on the Square
posts.date: June 25, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Here's the scoop, friends. The squares are humming, a fresh beach bar just opened, and the summer hours mean the music starts a little later and runs a little longer. Pour something cold and let me walk you through your weekend.

Quick note before we dance: through August, nightly music on the squares runs 6 to 10 p.m., not the old 5 to 9. Happy Hour still holds at 5 to 6. So you've got time for dinner first. I'm already planning my Saturday around it. (The Villages Entertainment)

What to do this weekend

Friday night on the squares. Take your pick. Spanish Springs has Fancy Reagan, Lake Sumter Landing turns into a dance party with CLUB CTRL featuring DJ Lu-S, and Brownwood brings The Brothers Jukebox. All free, all 6 to 10. (square schedule) My tip: eat early at Lake Sumter, grab a patio table by the water, then drift toward the music. Those waterfront tables fill up fast once the band starts.

Saturday is the big one. A real Villages favorite is back at Lake Sumter Landing — Rocky and The Rollers, 6 to 10. Twenty-seven years playing here and they still pack the square. Trust me on this one, get there early for a spot. Over at Spanish Springs you'll find Gravity Parade, and Brownwood has The Fire Rhythms Band. (square schedule)

Want a seat and air conditioning? 3DN — The Ultimate 3 Dog Nite Tribute plays the Savannah Center on Saturday, 7 to 8:30 p.m. They run through all 21 of Three Dog Night's Top 40 hits — “Joy to the World,” “Mama Told Me Not to Come,” “Shambala,” the whole songbook. Tickets start around $35. (show details) I sent my own neighbor to their last one and she came home singing.

Sunday, ease into it. Lake Sumter Landing has The Dave Capp Project, Spanish Springs the Justin Heet Band, and Brownwood winds down with 5.0.1. playing blues and soul, all 6 to 10. (square schedule) And if you like your evening smoother, More Jazz presents the Rick Steuart Quartet at Colony Cottage Recreation Center, starting 6 p.m. (event listing) A glass of wine and a little jazz on a Sunday — you're welcome.

Where to eat near the music. Lake Sumter is my easy answer because you can stroll right from dinner to the band. If you're at Brownwood, do an early bite and stay for the show. And here's a happy thought for Saturday morning — the Brownwood Farmers Market runs on the square, so you can grab fresh finds before the heat sets in. (Brownwood June calendar)

What's new

A new beach bar in Middleton. Say hello to Zunzibar, now open in downtown Middleton on the waterfront. It's a laid-back, beachy spot serving African, Caribbean, and Mediterranean flavors — think award-winning wings, fresh seafood, and tropical cocktails, with that big downtown water view. (Villages-News · Middleton) I haven't been yet, so I won't oversell it — but a frozen drink by the water in June? I'll be finding out soon. Tell 'em Susan sent you.

The new Walmart is open. The big Walmart on County Road 466 in Lady Lake opened its doors Wednesday, and folks were lined up early. (Villages-News) Not glamorous, I know, but a closer grocery run is a closer grocery run. Worth knowing which side of town you're on now.

A second ALDI is coming. The discount grocer announced an opening date for its second Villages-area store at La Plaza Grande. (Villages-News) If you're an ALDI quarter-for-the-cart person like me, this one's good news.

That's the honest list this week. I only put it in if I could check it, so if your favorite event isn't here, it just means I couldn't confirm the date in time — not that nothing's happening. When in doubt, I leave it out.

So that's your weekend. Music every night, a new spot to try, and Rocky and The Rollers to get you off your chair Saturday. Save me a seat by the water.

See you around the square,
— Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Music, Bingo & a Cold One
posts.date: June 22, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Well, friends, we made it through another hot one. Here's the scoop on the weekend that just wrapped, and trust me, the squares did not disappoint.

Friday night I had a choice to make, and so did you. Every square had a band going at 6:00. Over at Brownwood Paddock Square, it was Eighteen87 cranking out the hits. Lake Sumter Landing had Blue Stone Circle, the ultimate party band, rock to reggae to Top 40. Spanish Springs pulled out the big guns with Rocky and The Rollers, a Villages favorite for 27 years now. Sawgrass Grove had Zee-R Band, and Eastport's main stage gave us The Edge Of Rock. Five squares, five bands, one happy town.

I parked my cart at Lake Sumter and stayed put. No regrets.

Saturday & Sunday on the squares

Saturday I bounced back to the lake for The Voodoo Gypsies, a classic rock cover band out of Central Florida. They play the good stuff, '60s through '80s, the songs you already know every word to. If you wanted to dance instead, Brownwood went full club mode with CLUB CTRL featuring DJ Lu-S. Lights, beats, the works.

Sunday wound things down sweet. Lake Sumter brought back September Dogs, that female-fronted four-piece with the big layered vocals. And Brownwood closed the weekend with Sheila & The Sound, running everything from Aretha to Journey. By the last song, half the square was singing along.

Beat the heat

Here's a little something worth knowing if you've been melting out there. The squares moved their summer hours. Through August 31, the bands now play 6:00 to 10:00 PM instead of 5:00 to 9:00. Happy hour stays put at 5:00. Smart move, honestly. So if you've been skipping nights because the afternoon felt like a furnace, come a little later. The good stuff starts at six now.

And speaking of beating the heat, the bar huts are pouring a Tequila Sunrise this June while supplies last. Eight bucks for a single, ten-fifty for a double. I had one Saturday between sets. It did the job. You're welcome. (bar huts)

Who-knew note

For my catalogue folks always asking what to do around here. The POA has bingo night coming up at the Everglades Recreation Center. It's an easy, friendly way to meet a few neighbors if you're new in town. I've sent more than one new resident their way, and they always come back grinning. Tell 'em Susan sent you.

One more thing that made me smile. Villages-News ran a sweet piece on a couple here who just hit 70 years of marriage. Seventy! That's the kind of story that reminds me why I love this place.

The bottom line

I'll be straight with you, since I always am. It was a quieter weekend on the news front. No big festival, no grand opening I could confirm. So this week the squares carried the show, and that's just fine by me. Some weekends, good music and a cold drink are the whole point.

If you missed it all, don't fret. The bands roll on every single night, six to ten, all summer long. Pick a square, grab a seat, and let somebody else do the singing.

See you around the square,
— Susan

posts.title: Your Villages Weekend Recap: Storms, Squares & a Steakhouse on the Way
posts.date: June 15, 2026 · By Susan Whitfield, Villages insider
posts.body:
Well, friends, summer showed up and brought the heat. Here's the scoop on the weekend that just wrapped.

It was a classic June stretch — sunshine in the morning, then those low-to-mid 90s and a few afternoon thunderstorms rolling through. Saturday topped out near the mid-90s with scattered storms, and Sunday wasn't far behind. (weather.com) If the music felt like it started later than usual, you weren't imagining it. The squares are on summer hours — 6 to 10 p.m. now through August 31 — to dodge the worst of the heat. Happy hour still runs 5 to 6. (The Villages Entertainment)

Music on the squares

Brownwood is the one I can vouch for this weekend. Saturday night, DeadLanders took the Paddock Square stage — a DeLand band that leans country, classic and southern rock. Good boot-tapping stuff. Sunday, Beauty & The Beats closed things out with a '70s, '80s and '90s mix — the legends, the chart-toppers, and a few one-hit wonders you forgot you loved. (Brownwood lineup)

A little Susan honesty: the nightly calendars roll forward fast, so by Monday the Friday and Saturday names at Lake Sumter Landing and Spanish Springs had already cycled off the public page. Rather than guess, I'll point you to the live lineups so you can plan the week ahead — both Lake Sumter Landing and Brownwood keep theirs updated. Easiest way to never miss your favorite band.

A sip worth knowing

Heading to the bar huts this month? The June feature is a Tequila Sunrise — $8 single, $10.50 double, while supplies last. Pretty in the cup and easy on a warm night. (bar huts) I sent my own neighbor for one Saturday. She approved.

On the dining radar

One for the foodies. A new spot is on the horizon at the Woodlands Championship Golf Course: Luxe Steakhouse & Cellar, announced back in late March. It's the latest from Jack Suleiman, the same name behind RedSauce over at Lake Sumter Landing — so the bar's set high. No opening date yet (they say watch your Vmail), but steaks with a view of the greens? I'll be there. (The Villages — Shopping & Dining)

Who-knew note

Saturday-morning treasure hunters had a good one. There was a neighborhood garage sale Friday and Saturday over in the Village of Calumet Grove, on SE 171st Horseshoe Lane, 7:30 to 12:30. (Villages-News.com) The early birds always get the good stuff — that's just the law of the land here. Watch the Villages-News listings and the Daily Sun calendar if you like a good Saturday rummage.

The bottom line

Quieter, hotter weekend on the squares — the kind where you sip something cold, catch a band after the sun drops, and let the storms pass. I kept this one to what I could actually confirm, because I'd rather tell you the truth than fill the page. There's a steakhouse coming, the music plays every night, and summer's just getting started.

Now go enjoy yourself.

See you around the square,
— Susan
